items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: One of them was George Bach K., whom I stopped to see in Philadelphia in 1940, fall of 1940.

ctx.x: This is an interview with Bill Russell at Seminar Room 2 in the Harvard Tilton Memorial Library at Tulane University. This is Rio 1, the date is September 4th, 1962.

We'd been talking about some of the, this is Bill Russell again, some of the musicians that I'd interviewed at various times preparing for the book Jazz Man, and other times after that, that we weren't able to talk to because most of them are dead now. We weren't able to interview them for our Jazz Archive directly here. One of them was George Bach K., whom I stopped to see in Philadelphia in 1940, fall of 1940. The actual date was December 15th, 1940, on the way when I was moving to Pittsburgh. And he was…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: But I saw him in Philadelphia then. After the book Jazzmen was published, I interviewed him on the way to Pittsburgh after I left New York.

ctx.x: Well, maybe you could correct him.

A footnote or something like that. Yes, sort of evaluate some of that, too. I'd rather do that and not take a lot of time on the tape now to do that. And they're not in a condition to be photostadded or Xerox or whatever it is. Another man who's dead now, Buddy Christian, an outstanding banjo and guitar player from New Orleans, who also played piano here and also in New York. And he played on quite a few of the Clarence Williams Hot Five. And what are they called? Blue Five, excuse me. Anyway, he's been dead for…
